title: Building a Cube That Remembers Being Pushed
concept_layer: soft bodies as spring-mass lattices; stiffness, damping, pressure as the three knobs of elasticity; deformation as negotiation
domain_deferred: muscle simulation / inverse kinematics → swarm + ML sequences

capture_leaks.rigid_topology: The mesh topology doesn’t change — vertices move but connectivity is fixed. Tearing, splitting, merging all require changing topology at runtime, which SoftBody3D can’t do.
capture_leaks.homogeneous_material: One stiffness value covers the entire cube. Real bodies have variable stiffness (bone vs muscle vs skin). Composite materials need multiple SoftBody3Ds or a custom solver.
capture_leaks.no_rest_shape_memory: The cube remembers its original shape via spring rest-lengths, but it doesn’t remember deformation history. Plastic deformation (clay) requires updating rest-lengths mid-simulation.
capture_leaks.no_self_collision: This jelly passes through itself. Bunching, compression, or folding into itself breaks down. Self-collision requires spatial hashing, deferred.
capture_leaks.explicit_integration: The solver uses explicit time integration, which becomes unstable at high stiffness. Implicit solvers (used in real VFX) are outside the scope.

limit: A cube that jiggles. Three sliders control the physics. The artifact captures elasticity as a felt, tunable property — rigid vs liquid is a continuum, not a binary. What it refuses: topology change, material heterogeneity, plastic memory, self-collision, large deformations at high speed. Each is a door that opens later in the sequence.

grammar_alignment.note: jelly_cube teaches deform (change shape under force) and spring_mass (the underlying mesh topology). Cloth is an anisotropic spring_mass; reaction_diffusion is a chemical analog of deformation. All softbodies operations are variations on 'respond to local perturbation.'

biome_alignment.note: The 'soft' catalyst lets the player turn any rigid form in the biome into a soft body. Vegetation now bends under contact. Creatures have squishy contact with the world. This is where the biome stops feeling like infrastructure and starts feeling like a body.

stages.title: From generation to response
stages.thinking: Procgen generated populations; genetic programming bred them toward fitness. But every creature was still a rigid piece of geometry. Now we give those bodies the ability to yield. Not 'what shape am I' but 'how do I respond when touched.' Softness is not a shape — it’s a behavior. This sequence adds the behavioral layer to everything that came before.
stages.code:
# Fractal_Recursion: geometry from self-calls
# PG_Genetic_Evolution: geometry from evolved genomes
# Both produce rigid forms — geometry that is.
#
# Soft bodies: geometry that RESPONDS.
# Push it, it yields.
# Let go, it recovers.
# Squeeze it, it squishes.
#
# The form is no longer a noun — it's a verb.
# What it IS is less important than what it DOES when touched.

stages.title: SoftBody3D — Godot's built-in cloth-mesh physics
stages.thinking: Godot provides SoftBody3D: a mesh where every vertex is a particle connected to neighbors by springs. Pinned points stay fixed; free points swing under forces (gravity, collisions). This is the primitive we build on. Not implementing the springs ourselves — using the engine's solver — so the map is about TUNING the physics, not writing it.
stages.code:
extends Node3D
class_name JellyCube

@export_range(0.1, 1.0, 0.01) var cube_size: float = 0.3
@export_range(1, 8) var subdivisions: int = 4

var _soft_body: SoftBody3D
var _mesh_instance: MeshInstance3D
var _material: StandardMaterial3D

func _ready() -> void:
	_setup_soft_body()

func _setup_soft_body() -> void:
	_soft_body = SoftBody3D.new()
	_soft_body.mesh = _create_cube_mesh(cube_size, subdivisions)
	_soft_body.total_mass = 0.5
	add_child(_soft_body)

stages.title: Stiffness — rigid to liquid
stages.thinking: Stiffness is the spring constant between vertices. Near 0: springs are weak, the cube collapses under its own weight into a puddle. Near 1: springs are rigid, the cube barely yields. The sweet spot — where jelly lives — is around 0.3 to 0.6. This is the critical parameter. Change it with a slider, feel the material change from solid to slime without touching the geometry. One number. Infinite materials.
stages.code:
@export_range(0.0, 1.0, 0.01) var stiffness: float = 0.5:
	set(value):
		stiffness = value
		if _soft_body:
			_soft_body.linear_stiffness = value

# linear_stiffness maps directly to spring constants
#   0.0 → puddle
#   0.2 → tofu
#   0.5 → jelly
#   0.8 → rubber
#   1.0 → nearly rigid
#
# One property, a whole spectrum of material.

stages.title: Damping — how fast oscillation dies
stages.thinking: Without damping, a poke causes the cube to jiggle forever (in theory). Real materials dissipate energy — that’s damping. Low damping: long, playful wobbles. High damping: thick, sluggish response like thick honey. Damping and stiffness together define the feel. The same stiffness with different damping gives different characters — trampoline vs mattress vs mud.
stages.code:
@export_range(0.0, 1.0, 0.01) var damping: float = 0.1:
	set(value):
		damping = value
		if _soft_body:
			_soft_body.damping_coefficient = value

# damping_coefficient is energy loss per frame
#   0.01 → long wobble (trampoline)
#   0.1  → natural settle (jelly)
#   0.5  → sluggish (honey)
#   0.9  → instant death (sand)
#
# Damping is the material's memory of fatigue.

stages.title: Pressure — inflate to balloon, deflate to cloth
stages.thinking: SoftBody3D has a pressure_coefficient that simulates internal gas. Positive pressure inflates — the cube becomes a balloon straining outward. Zero pressure: the cube is free to collapse if stiffness is low. Negative (or the absence of inflation): it drapes like cloth. With three sliders (stiffness, damping, pressure) you cover trampolines, balloons, jellyfish, pillows, slime, and sheets. Three knobs, a material library.
stages.code:
@export_range(0.0, 5.0, 0.05) var pressure: float = 1.0:
	set(value):
		pressure = value
		if _soft_body:
			_soft_body.pressure_coefficient = value

# Combined material space (stiffness, damping, pressure):
#   (0.6, 0.1, 2.5)  → bouncy balloon
#   (0.5, 0.1, 1.0)  → default jelly
#   (0.2, 0.3, 0.0)  → drapey cloth
#   (0.9, 0.7, 0.0)  → rigid with slight give
#   (0.0, 0.5, 0.0)  → collapsing puddle

stages.title: Translucent material — see what you’re deforming
stages.thinking: The cube is colored with alpha < 1 so you can see through it. Touch it and watch the near vertices displace while the far vertices follow through the spring network. Without translucency, you’d only see the surface wiggle; with it, you see the propagation. Color as transparency is a teaching tool: it makes invisible physics visible.
stages.code:
@export var jelly_color: Color = Color(0.2, 0.9, 0.5, 0.8):
	set(value):
		jelly_color = value
		if _material:
			_material.albedo_color = value

func _make_material() -> StandardMaterial3D:
	var m = StandardMaterial3D.new()
	m.albedo_color = jelly_color  # alpha < 1
	m.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
	m.metallic = 0.2
	m.roughness = 0.3
	return m

# The translucent cube reveals the elastic network.
# Poke one side — see the wave propagate through.
# Physics made visible.

stages.title: Three sliders + color cycle button
stages.thinking: RackTemplates panel with sliders for stiffness, damping, pressure. A push button for color cycling (green → pink → blue → green) so the player can taste different palette moods. A reset button restores defaults. The panel is the interface to the physics. Each slider tick triggers the setter that updates the live SoftBody3D — no rebuild, no pause. The jelly jiggles during your tune.
stages.code:
func _create_controls() -> void:
	var RackTpl = load("res://commons/audio/rack_templates/RackTemplates.gd")
	var panel = RackTpl.create_panel("JELLY PHYSICS", [
		[{"type": "slider_h", "label": "STIFF", "default": stiffness}],
		[{"type": "slider_h", "label": "DAMP",  "default": damping}],
		[{"type": "slider_h", "label": "PRESS", "default": pressure / 5.0}],
		[{"type": "button", "label": "COLOR"}, {"type": "button", "label": "RESET"}],
	])
	panel.position = Vector3(0, -0.2, 0.4)
	panel.rotation_degrees.x = -25
	add_child(panel)

stages.title: Give it identity
stages.thinking: The jelly cube knows what it is. Not a toy — a demonstration that elasticity is a NEGOTIATION. The cube has internal forces (springs); your hands have external forces (collision); the deformation is where they meet. The artifact refuses topology change, plastic memory, self-collision. But what it offers — tunable softness, visible propagation, three-parameter material space — is enough to teach that matter is not rigid-or-liquid but a field of responses.
stages.code:
# @identity
# essence: SoftBody3D with spring-mass physics — stiffness, damping, and pressure_coefficient govern deformation response
# desire: to let you poke a translucent cube and feel its resistance change under your hands as you drag sliders between rigid and liquid
# critical_parameter: stiffness — at 0 the cube collapses into a puddle, at 1 it barely yields, the sweet spot between is where jelly lives
# triggers: hand collision with the SoftBody3D surface causes real-time vertex displacement; pressure slider inflates or deflates the volume
# emerges: at low stiffness and high pressure the cube becomes a breathing balloon; at low pressure it drapes over the pedestal like cloth
# needs: slider_horizontal [has] (stiffness, damping, pressure); push_button [has] (color cycle, reset); Label3D [has]
# relationships: introduces spring-mass foundation before cloth_straps and soft_mushroom; contrasts with rounded_softbody_test which adds strain visualization
# truth: elasticity is not a property of the object — it is a negotiation between the object's internal forces and whatever touches it
